_comment: ETO (Total ETO) source configuration for the Vendor Scorecard.
Every column the queries emit is declared here as a SQL expression, so a column
whose real name differs from the assumption can be corrected in this file WITHOUT
editing SQL. Entries set to null emit a typed NULL and keep the column contract
intact -- EXCEPT for the columns listed in EtoRepository.LOAD_BEARING, where a null
would silently kill a component or empty the whole dataset. Those are refused.
verified  - named in ETO_SCHEMA_MAP.md or a prior live probe against production
likely    - strongly implied by prior discovery, not directly confirmed
probe     - assumption; run tools/eto_schema_probe.py and correct before use
Read-only. This pipeline never writes to ETO.
PLACEHOLDER VALUES. The Excel prototype scored 23,344 PO lines AFTER cleaning;
vwPurchaseOrderDetails holds ~160,803. The extract was scoped by something nobody
has characterised, and these settings are a guess at it -- the not-sent backlog is
only ~4.5% of headers, so these three filters land nowhere near 23,344.
Set scope_confirmed to true once probe section D has settled the real scope.
Until then EtoRepository warns on every load.

purchase_orders._aliases: poh=PO header, pod=PO detail, rls=receiver log summed, im=item master, pj=projects
_part_note: vwPurchaseOrderDetails carries ItemID and ItemDescription, not a part number.
part_number therefore comes from the item master through the declared FK
pod.ItemID -> tblEngItemMaster.ItemID, using the SAME expression as the items
dataset -- so the PO part key and the Item Master part key cannot disagree,
which is exactly what lead-time matching depends on.
purchase_orders._receipt_note: last_receipt_date and received_qty are overridden at build time by options.last_receipt_source / options.received_qty_source; the values here are the receiver-log defaults
purchase_orders._additive: not consumed by the current pipeline; the migration path depends on them

ncrs._aliases: nc=vwNonConformances, ncl=vwNonConformanceList, ncc=costing, org=origin lookup, poh=PO header
ncrs.title: nc.Title
ncrs._additive: the exact-key supplier path that replaces name parsing

items._note: part_number here MUST use the same expression as purchase_orders.part_number

vendors._aliases: co=tblCompany, sup=tblSupplier (always LEFT JOINed so its columns are usable in every scope)
vendors._additive: supplier extension attributes; not consumed today

verified: all object names in sources (vwPurchaseOrderHeader 48 cols, vwPurchaseOrderDetails 36 cols)
poh / pod: PurchaseCurr, PurchaseCurrRate (on BOTH views; header used here)
pod.ProjectID, SpecID, PurchaseQty, PurchaseUOM, PurchasePrice, ExtendedPrice
pod.Received (decimal qty, NOT NULL), DateRequired, DateRevised, ItemID, ItemDescription
nc header cols on the view: SpecID (float NOT NULL), ItemID, Quantity, QuantityRejected,
nc view resolved names: PartNumber, SupplierID/Supplier, CustomerID/Customer,
NonConformanceCustom5 caption = 'Target Date' (Custom1..8 = 2 text / 2 decimal / 2 datetime / 2 bit)
im.EstimatedLeadTime keyed on ItemID - and EMPTY on every item
likely: poh.PurchasePrinted / PurchaseEmailed - verified on tblPurchaseOrderHeader, not on the view
note ETO's own urpNonConformanceSupplierImpact uses 'CompanyCity' via a display UDF)
inv.QtyOnHand aggregated per ItemID from vwInventory
probe: im.ItemCompanyID as the item number - LOAD-BEARING: drives part_number on BOTH datasets
item master: uom, category, list_price, revision, lpp, preferred_supplier,
po_part_number, order_number, ncr_hours - none is consumed today
